sources.author: Harrison Chase
sources.headline: Co-founder & CEO @ LangChain
sources.post_summary: Discussed the rapid evolution of AI agents moving from research prototypes to production systems. Highlighted new tooling patterns around memory, tool use, and evaluation that LangChain is releasing to help teams ship reliable agents faster.

sources.author: Simon Willison
sources.headline: Independent AI researcher & creator of Datasette
sources.post_summary: Shared practical insights on building lightweight AI automation scripts for developers using local models and simple orchestration. Emphasized avoiding over-engineered agent frameworks when simple prompt chaining suffices for most internal tools.

sources.author: Clemens Tiedt
sources.headline: Head of AI Infrastructure @ Scale AI
sources.post_summary: Posted about the current bottlenecks in AI infrastructure, particularly GPU scheduling and data loading pipelines. Shared internal metrics showing how small improvements in orchestration yielded 3x throughput gains for large training jobs.

sources.author: Santiago Valdarrama
sources.headline: AI Engineer & Educator
sources.post_summary: Explained a minimal agent architecture using open source components that developers can run on a single machine. Focused on the importance of explicit state machines over vague 'agent loops' for maintainable automation.

sources.author: Elena Vasquez
sources.headline: Head of Revenue Operations at Ramp
sources.post_summary: Discussed how her team built an internal GTM engineering function that reduced lead-to-opportunity time by 40%. Emphasized the importance of embedding data engineers directly into revenue teams rather than relying on centralized IT.

sources.author: Marcus Chen
sources.headline: Founder & CEO at Clay
sources.post_summary: Shared lessons from scaling outbound automation at Clay, including how they use enrichment + intent data to trigger hyper-personalized sequences. Warned against over-automation that removes human judgment from the sales process.

sources.author: Priya Sharma
sources.headline: VP of Sales Operations at Notion
sources.post_summary: Explained how Notion's revops team built a content-to-pipeline attribution model that connects blog posts and webinars directly to closed revenue. Highlighted the need for clean data pipelines between marketing and sales systems.

sources.author: David Okoro
sources.headline: GTM Engineer at OpenAI
sources.post_summary: Wrote about building internal tooling that automates account research and buying signal detection for the enterprise sales team. Stressed the value of treating GTM processes like product engineering with version control and testing.

sources.author: Rachel Torres
sources.headline: Director of Content Strategy at Gong
sources.post_summary: Detailed how Gong's content team shifted from top-of-funnel blogs to bottom-of-funnel enablement assets that directly support sales conversations. Shared metrics showing 3x increase in content-assisted deal velocity.

sources.author: Arjun Mahadevan
sources.headline: Founder & Engineer @ Tldv | Ex-Google
sources.post_summary: Shared the journey of building and shipping a new AI meeting tool feature in 10 days as a solo technical founder. Highlighted the importance of user feedback loops and cutting scope ruthlessly to launch fast.

sources.author: Danny Postma
sources.headline: Founder of Headlime & 2X acquired startups
sources.post_summary: Posted about pivoting from a failed SaaS to a new AI product, detailing the exact metrics that triggered the pivot and how he validated the new idea with 40 customer interviews in two weeks.

sources.author: Vic Vijayakumar
sources.headline: Solo Founder building in public | Prev. Microsoft
sources.post_summary: Documented week 3 of building a developer tool in public, sharing code snippets, user sign-up numbers, and lessons on pricing strategy after getting first 50 paid users.

sources.author: Sara Dietschy
sources.headline: Founder & Creator | Career pivot from marketing to tech founder
sources.post_summary: Wrote about transitioning from marketing into full-time indie development, including how she learned to code while shipping her first product and the community support that helped her stay consistent.

sources.author: Alex Finn
sources.headline: Solo developer shipping side projects | Ex-Amazon
sources.post_summary: Shared the launch of his third micro-SaaS, breaking down the tech stack choices, how he got initial traction through Twitter and LinkedIn, and revenue numbers after 30 days.
